title: Electronegativity Tug of War Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A charged comb bends a stream of water, salt breaks into ions, and oil and water refuse to mix. Behind all three is one hidden tug of war: atoms pulling on the electrons they share. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 3, Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties) we see what electronegativity is and why it changes across the periodic table.

You will see hydrogen chloride share a pair of electrons that slides towards chlorine, and the Pauling scale that sets fluorine at 4.0. On the molecule bench, an atom shrinks from lithium (1.0) to fluorine (4.0) across period 2, then grows with new shells down group 17 (F 4.0, Cl 3.0, Br 2.8, I 2.5), while the pull readout and bar charts update live. We explain the trend link by link (more protons, smaller atom, shared pair closer, stronger pull), connect it to metals and non-metals, rank the C-F, C-O and C-Cl bonds by their electronegativity gap, and check period 3 (Na 0.9 to Cl 3.0). Then the exam trap that mixes up electronegativity with electron gain enthalpy, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 34 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
